question.text: A trader buys Nifty futures at 22,000 and deposits Rs. 1,50,000 as initial margin. On Day 1, the settlement price is 22,200 (lot size 25). The Day 1 daily MTM settlement entry is:

answer.text: Debit: Bank or Deposit for MTM Margin Account Rs. 5,000; Credit: Mark-to-Market Margin Account Rs. 5,000
Debit: Bank Rs. 5,000; Credit: Sales Revenue Rs. 5,000
Debit: Initial Margin Rs. 5,000; Credit: Profit Reserve Rs. 5,000
No entry until the position is squared off

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the NISM Series VIII workbook (page 187), the daily MTM receipt is calculated as (22,200 - 22,000) x 25 = Rs. 5,000. The journal entry debits "Bank or Deposit for MTM Margin Account" Rs. 5,000 and credits the "Mark-to-Market Margin Account" Rs. 5,000. P&L recognition is reserved for final settlement or squaring off per page 189. The Trap: Crediting "Profit on Futures" on the daily MTM step conflates daily settlement with final P&L recognition; the calculation of Rs. 5,000 is correct, but the credit account is the MTM Margin Account, not a P&L account. Note: Source: NISM Series VIII workbook, pages 187 and 189.
